deck: Table Rock and Taneycomo, written like a fishing magazine — two waters, one week, nothing invented on the outdoor desk.

play.title: Pink worm, two-pound, no hero set.
play.body: Taneycomo in this clarity punishes heavy line and a hard hookset. Let them eat. Sweep.

season.name: Dog days
season.why: This is the hard season on the White River system, and it is also when the fishermen who live here quietly catch fish. Thermocline is set. Shad are deep. Table Rock surface is in the 80s. Taneycomo is still 50-degree tailwater.
tips: Fish the first 45 minutes like it matters. After that, put the topwater away.
Table Rock: 15–35 feet, electronics on. You are looking for bait, not banks.
Taneycomo: two- to six-pound test, pink Power Worm, no hero hookset.
MDC wants spotted bass harvested on Table Rock. Keep the spots. Put the 12-to-20-inch rainbows back.
Noon in August is not a fishing hour. Night on the points is a different lake.
License 16–64, plus a trout permit for Taneycomo. Bass Pro at the Landing sells both.

body: Warm surface water (82–86°F), improving clarity, and the ongoing drawdown have pushed bass, walleye, and crappie tighter to deeper main-lake structure and points. Fish are holding on offshore rock piles, brush, roll-offs, channel swings, and main-lake points in 20–30 ft. Football jigs and drop-shots are producing quality fish (including solid smallmouth) while covering water with electronics separates the good days from the slow ones. Recent 9/10 trips reported over 30 bass plus keeper walleye in mornings, with another 40+ bass afternoon; the fall bite is building. Low-light topwater around swings and points can still pay off, though darker colors appear better right now. Walleye remain productive on gravel points. It's a technical grind that rewards preparation and mobility as we edge closer to fall turnover — match the generation-driven conditions and the fish are there.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~12,600 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: The cold, clear tailwater fishery remains in solid late-summer form per recent 9/10 reports (40 rainbows on jigs and pink worms) and September patterns. Low morning flows create the best windows for wading anglers and dock fishermen from just below the dam downstream. When generation ramps, shift to boat drifts targeting current seams, breaks, eddies, and deeper holding water. Pink Power Worms have been the standout bait — fished on split-shot rigs or under a float — alongside micro jigs, midges, scuds, eggs, and nightcrawlers. Light line and clean presentations are essential in the gin-clear water; rainbows make up the bulk of catches with some quality fish (including 19–23" range in recent weeks). Slot limits apply in upper reaches (12–20" rainbows must be released). Dock fishing shines during minimal flow. Always call 866-494-1993 for the live SWPA generation schedule before heading o

## Why open this tomorrow Overnight shifts in the SWPA generation schedule, any early-September cool front, rainfall in the White River basin, or continued lake-level movement could reposition fish or open new bite windows on both waters. Taneycomo tactics flip the instant the turbines start or stop, while Table Rock offshore patterns often sharpen with small changes in clarity, temperature, or post-storm conditions as fall approaches. Check tablerocklakelevel.com, the USACE gage, and the SWPA hotline first thing — tomorrow could reward a completely different timing or presentation than today.

Taneycomo tactics and patterns carried from recent FishingBooker reports (9/10: 40 rainbows on jigs/pink worms/split-shot, strong numbers), John Sappington September overview (low overnight/early flows favoring wading, pink worms/micro jigs), and Extreme Outdoors forecast.
